gap: No result ChatGPT got states how far HD-over-coax video actually carries on existing RG-59 cable when someone tests it. Mammoth Security says its tests reached about 1,000 ft for HD-CVI and HD-TVI on RG-59, against the 'over 1,500 ft' the makers claim.
standout_why: I compared against the two pages ChatGPT cited: Dahua's XVR7208A-4K-I3 product page (opened 2026-11-17) and Hikvision's DS-7208HQHI-S1/XT page. The Hikvision page redirected to hikvision.com and the fetch came back empty, so I judged it from the result title and Hikvision's usual product-page format. The other results are Dahua and Hikvision datasheets and product pages. Dahua's page gives only maker figures ('<15 W (without HDD)', format and resolution tables) and cites no independent test. None of the results gives a coax distance at all, measured or claimed. I found no lab or named-reviewer measurement of any candidate recorder itself: no wattage, bitrate, storage per day or detection accuracy for ANNKE, ZOSI, Viewtron, Dahua, Hikvision or UNV. So the finding is new but general. It is one installer's test with no method published, and it does not tell the candidates apart.
decides: It doesn't change which recorder to pick. It is a check to run before buying any of them. If the shopper's existing RG-59 runs are well under about 1,000 ft, an HD-CVI or HD-TVI camera should work on any of the hybrid DVRs listed. Near or past that length, plan for an amplifier or new cable rather than relying on the makers' 1,500 ft+ figure.

findings.label: Tested HD-CVI and HD-TVI range on RG-59 coax
findings.source_title: IP vs Analog Cameras (Mammoth Security blog, Eugene Klimaszewski, Founder & President, published 2022-02-28)
findings.note: Quote: 'CVI and TVI both claim "over 1,500" feet of range using RG-59 coax cable (and our tests validated a range of 1,000 feet)'. The page names no camera models, recorder, cable brand or pass/fail standard. AHD was not covered. Mammoth is an installer, not an independent lab. This is the only named test result I could source for this angle.

unsourced: Measured power draw (watts at the wall, with and without a hard drive) for any candidate DVR. I searched for reviewer or lab tests of ANNKE, ZOSI, Dahua, Hikvision and Viewtron hybrid DVRs and found only maker ratings and blog estimates.
Any named-reviewer or lab review with figures for ANNKE DR88, DR85 or DR165. Searches returned only retailer listings, Loox and Trustpilot buyer reviews, and no outlet test.
Any named-reviewer or lab review of ZOSI ZR08VMA or ZR16FK. I checked for PCMag, Tom's Guide, TechRadar, Security.org and SafeWise reviews and found none, only retailer and aggregator pages.
Independent tests of Dahua XVR or Hikvision Turbo HD recorders. IPVM's Dahua and Hikvision tests I found are of IP cameras and are paywalled. I found no IPVM recorder test with figures I could open.
Viewtron VT-DVR-8 measured performance. CCTV Camera Pros (the seller) gives distance and 4K frame-rate figures without any described test method, so I didn't count them as measurements.
The Gadgeteer's ANNKE DVR review (Dennis Moore, 2017-07-17, model DN81R by its image filenames) has no measured figures, only spec-sheet numbers. It is also an old model, not a current candidate.
I found no measured storage per day for any candidate. ZOSI's own calculator gives only maker estimates.
PVR Blog's 'Best HVR Systems for 2026: Tested Picks' (pvrblog.com/hvr/best/) could not be opened because of an SSL certificate error, so I couldn't check whether it contains any measured figures.
